findings.where: Phone hero, the portrait stand-in below the 'Get in touch' button
findings.fault: On the phone, Mark's portrait drops below the headline, the pitch and the button. It also shrinks to a box pushed to the right, with an empty strip of about 110 px on its left that nothing else on the page lines up with. On the first screen it reads as a stray panel that slid off its grid, not as a figure placed on purpose. It also puts the man after the ask, not beside it as on desktop.
findings.who_objects: Mark and a development-bank visitor reading on a phone. The brief wants the man himself to be seen. Here he arrives last, in a box that looks misaligned, so the hero feels less finished and less personal than the desktop one.

findings.where: Style tile below the hero, the section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' (right column) against 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' (left column), on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The labels are styled the same, but only the two right-column labels have a hairline rule under them. The left-column labels have none. Labels that look alike are treated differently, which breaks similarity. The tile's own rule for section headers is left unclear.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer, and Angélique when she adds a section. Both would copy the tile's header treatment, and the tile gives two answers.
